name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q01 - Addition of water to but-1-yne

questiontext.text: Addition of water to alkynes occurs in acidic medium and in the presence of \(\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}\) ions as a catalyst. Which of the following products will be formed on addition of water to but-1-yne under these conditions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hydration of alkynes in acidic medium in the presence of \(\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}\) ions (Kucherov's reaction) proceeds via Markovnikov's rule to form an enol intermediate, which rapidly tautomerises to the more stable carbonyl compound.

Step 2: Reaction Analysis
For but-1-yne (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C\equiv CH}\)), the internal carbon (\(\mathrm{C2}\)) has no hydrogen atom, while the terminal carbon (\(\mathrm{C1}\)) has one hydrogen atom. Upon addition of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group attaches to the more substituted carbon (\(\mathrm{C2}\)) and the \(-\mathrm{H}\) atom attaches to the terminal carbon (\(\mathrm{C1}\)), forming the enol \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C(OH)=CH_2}\).

Step 3: Tautomerisation and Conclusion
The enol intermediate undergoes keto-enol tautomerisation by shifting a proton from oxygen to \(\mathrm{C1}\) and shifting the \(\pi\)-bond to form a \(\mathrm{C=O}\) double bond, yielding butan-2-one (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C(=O)CH_3}\)).

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q02 - Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition reactions

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds is most reactive towards nucleophilic addition reactions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reactivity of carbonyl compounds towards nucleophilic addition increases with greater electrophilicity (partial positive charge) of the carbonyl carbon and decreases with steric hindrance around the carbonyl group.

Step 2: Electronic and Steric Evaluation
Alkyl groups exert an electron-donating \(+I\) effect and add steric bulk, both of which reduce reactivity. Aryl groups additionally donate electron density into the carbonyl group by resonance (\(+R\) effect), further decreasing the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon. Ketones have two alkyl/aryl groups, whereas aldehydes have only one.

Step 3: Conclusion
Among ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3-C(=O)H}\)), propanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3-C(=O)CH_3}\)), benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-C(=O)H}\)), and acetophenone (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-C(=O)CH_3}\)), ethanal has only one methyl group and no resonance deactivation, making it the least sterically hindered and most electrophilic, and therefore the most reactive towards nucleophilic addition.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q03 - Correct order of increasing acidic strength

questiontext.text: The correct order of increasing acidic strength is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acidic strength depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed after loss of a proton (\(\mathrm{H}^+\)). Greater delocalisation or dispersal of negative charge in the conjugate base leads to stronger acidity.

Step 2: Comparison of Conjugate Bases
Ethoxide ion (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2O^-}\)) is destabilised by the \(+I\) effect of the ethyl group, making ethanol the weakest acid. Phenoxide ion (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5O^-}\)) is stabilised by resonance over the benzene ring, making phenol more acidic than ethanol. Carboxylate ions are much more stable because the negative charge is delocalised over two equivalent electronegative oxygen atoms, so acetic acid is stronger than phenol. In chloroacetic acid, the electron-withdrawing \(-I\) effect of the chlorine atom further stabilises the chloroacetate ion.

Step 3: Conclusion
The correct order of increasing acidic strength is \(\text{Ethanol} < \text{Phenol} < \text{Acetic acid} < \text{Chloroacetic acid}\).

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q04 - Preparation of phenyl benzoate from phenol

questiontext.text: Compound \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{O}-\stackrel{\mathrm{O}}{\stackrel{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{Ph}\) can be prepared by the reaction of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phenols do not undergo direct esterification readily with carboxylic acids because the lone pair on oxygen is delocalised into the aromatic ring, reducing its nucleophilicity. Instead, phenols are acylated using more reactive acid chlorides in the presence of a mild base such as pyridine.

Step 2: Reaction Mechanism
Phenol reacts with benzoyl chloride (\(\mathrm{PhCOCl}\)) in the presence of pyridine to form phenyl benzoate (\(\mathrm{Ph-O-C(=O)-Ph}\)) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\). Pyridine acts as both a nucleophilic catalyst and a base to neutralise the \(\mathrm{HCl}\) formed during the reaction, shifting the equilibrium forward.

Step 3: Conclusion
Phenyl benzoate is prepared by the reaction of phenol and benzoyl chloride in the presence of pyridine.

answer.text: Phenol and benzoic acid in the presence of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\)
Phenol and benzoyl chloride in the presence of pyridine
Phenol and benzoyl chloride in the presence of \(\mathrm{ZnCl_2}\)
Phenol and benzaldehyde in the presence of palladium

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q05 - Reagent unreactive towards acetone and benzaldehyde

questiontext.text: The reagent which does not react with both, acetone and benzaldehyde.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fehling's solution is a mild oxidising agent (alkaline \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) complexed with tartrate ions) used specifically to test for aliphatic aldehydes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reagents
Sodium hydrogensulphite (\(\mathrm{NaHSO_3}\)), phenyl hydrazine (\(\mathrm{PhNHNH_2}\)), and Grignard reagents all undergo nucleophilic addition reactions with both aldehydes (including benzaldehyde) and methyl ketones (such as acetone). In contrast, ketones lack the aldehydic \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bond and are not oxidised by Fehling's solution, and aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde are stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring and also fail to reduce Fehling's solution.

Step 3: Conclusion
Fehling's solution does not react with either acetone or benzaldehyde.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q06 - Aldehyde not undergoing Cannizzaro reaction

questiontext.text: Cannizaro's reaction is not given by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cannizzaro's reaction is a base-induced disproportionation undergone only by aldehydes that do not possess any \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom. Aldehydes containing \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms undergo aldol condensation in the presence of base instead.

Step 2: Evaluation of Structures
1-Methylcyclohexanecarbaldehyde has a quaternary \(\alpha\)-carbon with no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen. Benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\)) has an \(\mathrm{sp^2}\) ring carbon at the \(\alpha\)-position with no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen. Formaldehyde (\(\mathrm{HCHO}\)) has no \(\alpha\)-carbon at all. Ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)) contains three \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms on its methyl group.

Step 3: Conclusion
Because \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\) possesses \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms, it does not give Cannizzaro's reaction.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q07 - Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde with KOH

questiontext.text: Which product is formed when the compound \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\) is treated with concentrated aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\) solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\)) lacks an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom, so on treatment with concentrated aqueous alkali (\(\mathrm{KOH}\)), it undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction (self-oxidation and self-reduction / disproportionation).

Step 2: Reaction Analysis
One molecule of benzaldehyde is oxidised to the carboxylate salt (potassium benzoate, \(\mathrm{C_6H_5COO^-K^+}\)), while a second molecule is reduced to the corresponding alcohol (benzyl alcohol, \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}\)):
\[2\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO} + \mathrm{KOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5COO^-K^+} + \mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}\]

Step 3: Conclusion
The products formed are potassium benzoate and benzyl alcohol.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q08 - Hydration of propyne and tautomerism

questiontext.text:
\[\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH} \xrightarrow[1\%\,\mathrm{HgSO_4}]{40\%\,\mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\text{Isomerisation}} \mathrm{CH_3-\underset{\substack{\parallel \\ \mathrm{O}}}{C}-CH_3}\]

Structure of 'A' and type of isomerism in the above reaction are respectively.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Hydration of Propyne
Propyne (\(\mathrm{CH_3-C\equiv CH}\)) reacts with water in the presence of \(40\%\,\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) and \(1\%\,\mathrm{HgSO_4}\) according to Markovnikov's rule. The \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group adds to the internal carbon (\(\mathrm{C2}\)) and \(-\mathrm{H}\) adds to the terminal carbon (\(\mathrm{C1}\)), forming the enol intermediate \(\mathrm{CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2}\).

Step 2: IUPAC Naming and Isomerism
The IUPAC name of \(\mathrm{CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2}\) is prop-1-en-2-ol. This enol spontaneously isomerises to propanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3}\)) via the migration of a proton from oxygen to carbon and shifting of the double bond, which is known as keto-enol tautomerism.

Step 3: Conclusion
Compound 'A' is prop-1-en-2-ol and the type of isomerism involved is tautomerism.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q09 - Grignard addition, dehydration, and hydroboration-oxidation

questiontext.text:
Compounds A and C in the following reaction are

\[\mathrm{CH_3CHO} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) }\mathrm{H_2O}]{\text{(i) }\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}} (\mathrm{A}) \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2SO_4},\,\Delta} (\mathrm{B}) \xrightarrow{\text{Hydroboration oxidation}} (\mathrm{C})\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of A, B, and C
1. Ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)) reacts with \(\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}\) followed by hydrolysis to give a secondary alcohol, propan-2-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3}\)), which is compound (A).
2. Heating propan-2-ol with \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) causes dehydration to form propene (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2}\)), which is compound (B).
3. Hydroboration-oxidation of propene results in anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond to yield a primary alcohol, propan-1-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)), which is compound (C).

Step 2: Comparison of A and C
Propan-2-ol (\(\mathrm{A}\)) and propan-1-ol (\(\mathrm{C}\)) have the same molecular formula (\(\mathrm{C_3H_8O}\)) and the same functional group (\(-\mathrm{OH}\)), but differ in the position of the hydroxyl group on the carbon chain.

Step 3: Conclusion
Compounds A and C are positional isomers.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q10 - Selective oxidation of methyl ketone via haloform

questiontext.text:
Which is the most suitable reagent for the following conversion?

\[\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-\overset{\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\parallel}}{C}-CH_3} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-\overset{\overset{\mathrm{O}}{\parallel}}{C}-OH}\]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Analysis
The reactant contains a methyl ketone group (\(-\mathrm{COCH_3}\)) as well as an alkene double bond (\(\mathrm{C=C}\)). The product is the corresponding carboxylic acid with one fewer carbon atom, while the \(\mathrm{C=C}\) double bond remains intact.

Step 2: Reagent Selection
The haloform (iodoform) reaction using \(\mathrm{I_2}\) and \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution selectively oxidises methyl ketones (\(\mathrm{R-CO-CH_3}\)) to carboxylate salts (\(\mathrm{R-COO^-Na^+}\), which yield carboxylic acids on acidification) along with iodoform (\(\mathrm{CHI_3}\)), without affecting the carbon-carbon double bond. Tollens' reagent does not oxidise ketones, benzoyl peroxide is a radical initiator, and \(\mathrm{Sn/NaOH}\) is not an oxidising reagent for this conversion.

Step 3: Conclusion
The most suitable reagent for this conversion is \(\mathrm{I_2}\) and \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q11 - Oxidation of butan-2-ol to butanone

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds will give butanone on oxidation with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Oxidation of primary alcohols with strong oxidising agents like alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) yields carboxylic acids, whereas oxidation of secondary alcohols yields ketones.

Step 2: Evaluation of Alcohols
Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol and oxidises to butanoic acid with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\). Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-CH_3}\)) and oxidises to the four-carbon ketone, butanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_3}\)).

Step 3: Conclusion
Butan-2-ol gives butanone on oxidation with alkaline \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) solution.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQI_MCQ_Q12 - Reagents used in Clemmensen reduction

questiontext.text: In Clemmensen Reduction carbonyl compound is treated with

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Clemmensen reduction converts the carbonyl group (\(>\mathrm{C=O}\)) of aldehydes and ketones into a methylene group (\(>\mathrm{CH_2}\)).

Step 2: Reagent Identification
The reaction is carried out using zinc amalgam (\(\mathrm{Zn-Hg}\)) and concentrated hydrochloric acid (\(\mathrm{HCl}\)). Nitric acid (\(\mathrm{HNO_3}\)) cannot be used because it is an oxidising acid, and sodium amalgam is not the Clemmensen reagent.

Step 3: Conclusion
In Clemmensen reduction, the carbonyl compound is treated with zinc amalgam + \(\mathrm{HCl}\).

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQII_MCQ_Q13 - Compounds not undergoing aldol condensation

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds do not undergo aldol condensation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Aldol condensation occurs in aldehydes and ketones that possess at least one \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom (a hydrogen attached to the carbon adjacent to the carbonyl group).

Step 2: Evaluation of Compounds
Ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CHO}\)) has three \(\alpha\)-hydrogens and propanone (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3}\)) has six \(\alpha\)-hydrogens, so both undergo aldol condensation. In benzaldehyde (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\)), the \(\alpha\)-carbon is part of the aromatic ring and has no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen. In 2,2-dimethylpropanal (\(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-CHO}\)), the \(\alpha\)-carbon is quaternary and carries no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen.

Step 3: Conclusion
Benzaldehyde and 2,2-dimethylpropanal do not contain any \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms and therefore do not undergo aldol condensation.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQII_MCQ_Q14 - Alkaline hydrolysis of phenyl benzoate

questiontext.text: Treatment of compound \(\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{O}-\stackrel{\mathrm{O}}{\stackrel{\parallel}{\mathrm{C}}}-\mathrm{Ph}\) with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution yields

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Esters undergo alkaline hydrolysis (saponification) when treated with aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to form the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid and the corresponding alcohol or phenol.

Step 2: Reaction Analysis
Phenyl benzoate (\(\mathrm{Ph-O-C(=O)-Ph}\)) hydrolyses in \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to give sodium benzoate (\(\mathrm{PhCOONa}\)) and phenol (\(\mathrm{PhOH}\)). Because phenol is acidic, it reacts further with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) in the alkaline medium to form sodium phenoxide (\(\mathrm{PhONa}\)).

Step 3: Conclusion
Treatment of phenyl benzoate with \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) solution yields sodium phenoxide and sodium benzoate.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQII_MCQ_Q15 - Conversions carried out by Clemmensen reduction

questiontext.text: Which of the following conversions can be carried out by Clemmensen Reduction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Clemmensen reduction uses \(\mathrm{Zn-Hg}\) and concentrated \(\mathrm{HCl}\) to completely reduce the carbonyl group (\(>\mathrm{C=O}\)) of aldehydes and ketones to a methylene group (\(>\mathrm{CH_2}\)), forming hydrocarbons.

Step 2: Evaluation of Conversions
Reducing benzaldehyde to benzyl alcohol stops at the alcohol stage and requires \(\mathrm{NaBH_4}\) or \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\), not Clemmensen reduction. Reducing benzoyl chloride to benzaldehyde is Rosenmund reduction (\(\mathrm{H_2/Pd-BaSO_4}\)). In contrast, Clemmensen reduction converts cyclohexanone (\(\mathrm{C_6H_{10}O}\)) into cyclohexane (\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}\)) and benzophenone (\(\mathrm{Ph_2C=O}\)) into diphenylmethane (\(\mathrm{Ph_2CH_2}\)).

Step 3: Conclusion
Cyclohexanone into cyclohexane and benzophenone into diphenyl methane can be carried out by Clemmensen reduction.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQII_MCQ_Q16 - Reactions increasing carbon chain length

questiontext.text: Through which of the following reactions number of carbon atoms can be increased in the chain?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
To increase the number of carbon atoms in a carbon chain, a reaction must form a new carbon-carbon (\(\mathrm{C-C}\)) bond.

Step 2: Evaluation of Reactions
In a Grignard reaction, a nucleophilic alkyl or aryl group from \(\mathrm{RMgX}\) attacks an electrophilic carbon (such as a carbonyl or \(\mathrm{CO_2}\)), forming a new \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond and lengthening the chain. In aldol condensation, two carbonyl molecules couple together via enolate attack to form a \(\beta\)-hydroxy carbonyl or \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated carbonyl compound with a longer carbon chain. In contrast, Cannizzaro's reaction is a disproportionation without \(\mathrm{C-C}\) bond formation, and the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction substitutes an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen with a halogen (\(-\mathrm{Cl}\) or \(-\mathrm{Br}\)) without adding carbon atoms.

Step 3: Conclusion
The number of carbon atoms in the chain can be increased through the Grignard reaction and aldol condensation.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQII_MCQ_Q17 - Methods for preparing benzophenone

questiontext.text: Benzophenone can be obtained by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Synthetic Routes
1. Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with benzoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) yields benzophenone (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CO-C_6H_5}\)).
2. Reaction of benzoyl chloride with diphenylcadmium (\(\mathrm{(C_6H_5)_2Cd}\)) also gives benzophenone cleanly because organocadmium reagents do not react further with ketones.
3. Reaction of benzoyl chloride with phenyl magnesium chloride (\(\mathrm{PhMgCl}\)) proceeds beyond the ketone to form triphenylmethanol unless special precautions are taken. Benzene with \(\mathrm{CO}\) and \(\mathrm{ZnCl_2}\) (without \(\mathrm{HCl}\)/Gattermann-Koch conditions) does not form benzophenone.

Step 2: Conclusion
Benzophenone can be obtained by reacting benzoyl chloride with benzene in the presence of \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\), or by reacting benzoyl chloride with diphenyl cadmium.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MCQII_MCQ_Q18 - Tetrahedral intermediate of nucleophilic addition

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the correct representation for intermediate of nucleophilic addition reaction to the given carbonyl compound (A)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The carbonyl carbon in compound (A) is \(\mathrm{sp^2}\) hybridised and trigonal planar. When a nucleophile (\(\mathrm{Nu^-}\)) attacks the carbonyl carbon, the hybridisation changes from \(\mathrm{sp^2}\) to \(\mathrm{sp^3}\), forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate.

Step 2: Stereochemical Analysis
Because the carbonyl group is planar, the nucleophile can attack from either face (front/top or back/bottom) with equal probability. Attack from one face places substituent \(a\) away (dashed wedge) and \(b\) towards the viewer (solid wedge), while attack from the opposite face places \(b\) away (dashed wedge) and \(a\) towards the viewer (solid wedge). Both tetrahedral representations are valid intermediates (enantiomeric when \(a \neq b\)), whereas the planar cross representations do not depict the tetrahedral \(\mathrm{sp^3}\) geometry.

Step 3: Conclusion
Both tetrahedral alkoxide intermediates showing dashed and wedged bonds for substituents \(a\) and \(b\) are correct representations.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MATCHING_Q38 - Match common names with IUPAC names

questiontext.text: Match the common names given in Column I with the IUPAC names given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Identification
1. Cinnamaldehyde has structure \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH=CH-CHO}\), which is a three-carbon aldehyde with a double bond at C2 and a phenyl group at C3, giving the IUPAC name 3-Phenylprop-2-enal.
2. Acetophenone is methyl phenyl ketone (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CO-CH_3}\)), which is named 1-Phenylethanone.
3. Valeraldehyde is the five-carbon straight-chain aldehyde (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CHO}\)), corresponding to Pentanal.
4. Acrolein is \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CHO}\), corresponding to Prop-2-enal.
5. Mesityl oxide is \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH-CO-CH_3}\), a five-carbon \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated ketone with a methyl substituent at C4, corresponding to 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MATCHING_Q39 - Match dicarboxylic acids with IUPAC names

questiontext.text: Match the acids given in Column I with their correct IUPAC names given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Identification of Dicarboxylic Acids
1. Phthalic acid is an aromatic dicarboxylic acid with two \(-\mathrm{COOH}\) groups at adjacent (1,2) positions on a benzene ring: Benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid.
2. Oxalic acid is the simplest dicarboxylic acid (\(\mathrm{HOOC-COOH}\)), containing two carbons: Ethane-1,2-dioic acid.
3. Succinic acid has four carbons (\(\mathrm{HOOC-(CH_2)_2-COOH}\)): Butane-1,4-dioic acid.
4. Adipic acid has six carbons (\(\mathrm{HOOC-(CH_2)_4-COOH}\)): Hexane-1,6-dioic acid.
5. Glutaric acid has five carbons (\(\mathrm{HOOC-(CH_2)_3-COOH}\)): Pentane-1,5-dioic acid.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MATCHING_Q40 - Match organic conversions with suitable reagents

questiontext.text: Match the reactions given in Column I with the suitable reagents given in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reagent Matching
1. Benzophenone is reduced to diphenylmethane (deoxygenation of \(-\mathrm{CO}-\) to \(-\mathrm{CH_2}-\)) by Clemmensen reduction using \(\mathrm{Zn(Hg)/Conc.\,HCl}\).
2. Benzaldehyde is converted to 1-phenylethanol by nucleophilic addition of a methyl group using the Grignard reagent \(\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}\) (followed by hydrolysis).
3. Cyclohexanone is reduced to cyclohexanol using the hydride reducing agent \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\).
4. Phenyl benzoate (an ester) is partially reduced to benzaldehyde using diisobutylaluminium hydride (\(\mathrm{DIBAL-H}\)).

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_MATCHING_Q41 - Match chemical reactions with their named reactions

questiontext.text: Match the example given in Column I with the name of the reaction in Column II.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identification of Named Reactions
1. Reduction of acetyl chloride with \(\mathrm{H_2}\) over \(\mathrm{Pd-C/BaSO_4}\) to ethanal is Rosenmund's reduction.
2. Disproportionation of benzaldehyde in \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate is Cannizaro's reaction.
3. Acylation of benzene with acetyl chloride in the presence of \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) to acetophenone is Friedel Crafts acylation.
4. \(\alpha\)-Bromination of a carboxylic acid with \(\mathrm{Br_2/Red\,P}\) is the HVZ reaction.
5. Partial reduction of acetonitrile with \(\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}\) followed by hydrolysis to ethanal is Stephen's reaction.
6. Base-catalysed self-condensation of ethanal to but-2-enal is Aldol condensation.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_AR_Q42 - Geometry and hybridisation of formaldehyde

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the following choices.

Assertion : Formaldehyde is a planar molecule.

Reason : It contains \(\mathrm{sp^2}\) hybridised carbon atom.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Formaldehyde (\(\mathrm{HCHO}\)) has a central carbon bonded to two hydrogen atoms and doubly bonded to one oxygen atom, with all four atoms lying in the same plane. Thus, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
The carbonyl carbon in formaldehyde forms three \(\sigma\)-bonds and one \(\pi\)-bond, so it is \(\mathrm{sp^2}\) hybridised with a trigonal planar geometry (bond angles close to \(120^\circ\)). Thus, the reason is correct and directly explains why formaldehyde is planar.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are correct and reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are wrong statements.
Assertion is correct statement but reason is wrong statement.
Assertion is wrong statement but reason is correct statement.
Assertion and reason both are correct statements but reason is not correct explanation of assertion.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_AR_Q43 - Oxidation of aldehydes and reduction of acids

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the following choices.

Assertion : Compounds containing \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) group are easily oxidised to corresponding carboxylic acids.

Reason : Carboxylic acids can be reduced to alcohols by treatment with \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Aldehydes (compounds containing the \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) group) possess an aldehydic \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bond that is readily oxidised to carboxylic acids even by mild oxidising agents such as Tollens' reagent or Fehling's solution. Thus, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols by strong reducing agents like \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\). Thus, the reason is also a correct statement, but it does not explain why aldehydes are easily oxidised.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are correct and reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are wrong statements.
Assertion is correct statement but reason is wrong statement.
Assertion is wrong statement but reason is correct statement.
Assertion and reason both are correct statements but reason is not correct explanation of assertion.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_AR_Q44 - Acidity of alpha-hydrogen in carbonyl compounds

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the following choices.

Assertion : The \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom in carbonyl compounds is less acidic.

Reason : The anion formed after the loss of \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom is resonance stabilised.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
The \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms in carbonyl compounds are significantly acidic (much more acidic than ordinary \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bonds in alkanes) due to the strong electron-withdrawing effect of the adjacent carbonyl group and resonance stabilisation of the conjugate base. Therefore, the assertion stating it is less acidic is wrong.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
After removal of an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen as \(\mathrm{H^+}\), the resulting enolate carbanion is stabilised by resonance with the carbonyl oxygen. Therefore, the reason is a correct statement.

answer.text: Assertion and reason both are correct and reason is correct explanation of assertion.
Assertion and reason both are wrong statements.
Assertion is correct statement but reason is wrong statement.
Assertion is wrong statement but reason is correct statement.
Assertion and reason both are correct statements but reason is not correct explanation of assertion.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_AR_Q45 - Cannizzaro reaction and reactivity of aromatic aldehydes

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the following choices.

Assertion : Aromatic aldehydes and formaldehyde undergo Cannizaro reaction.

Reason : Aromatic aldehydes are almost as reactive as formaldehyde.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Both aromatic aldehydes and formaldehyde lack \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms, so both undergo the Cannizzaro reaction in the presence of concentrated alkali. Thus, the assertion is correct.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Formaldehyde is far more reactive towards nucleophilic attack than aromatic aldehydes because formaldehyde has minimal steric hindrance and no electron-donating resonance from an aryl ring to reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon. Thus, the reason is a wrong statement.

name.text: CHEMISTRY_UNIT12_AR_Q46 - Tollens test for aldehydes and ketones

questiontext.text:
In the following question a statement of assertion followed by a statement of reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the following choices.

Assertion : Aldehydes and ketones, both react with Tollen's reagent to form silver mirror.

Reason : Both, aldehydes and ketones contain a carbonyl group.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Assertion
Aldehydes are easily oxidised by Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) to give a silver mirror, whereas ketones lack the aldehydic \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bond and do not react with Tollens' reagent. Therefore, the assertion is wrong.

Step 2: Evaluate the Reason
Both aldehydes and ketones contain the carbonyl functional group (\(>\mathrm{C=O}\)). Therefore, the reason is a correct statement.
